name: Stubai Glacier
kurzbeschreibung: The Stubai Glacier at up to 3,210 m in the Stubai Valley: Austria's largest glacier ski resort featuring the Top of Tyrol viewing platform and a walk-in ice cave.
beschreibung:
Overview

The monumental Stubai Glacier is located at the head of the Stubai Valley in the municipality of Neustift im Stubaital (Innsbruck-Land district) at snow-reliable elevations between 1,695 and 3,210 metres. As Austria's largest glacier ski area, it spans five distinct glaciers (Daunkogelferner, Eisjochferner, Windachferner, Fernauferner, and Gaiskarferner). Framed by 109 prominent peaks exceeding 3,000 metres in the Stubai Alps, the glacier is an internationally acclaimed winter sports hub as well as a captivating year-round alpine destination for nature lovers and families alike.

Route & Requirements

The state-of-the-art 3S Eisgratbahn gondola whisks guests from the valley floor directly to the Eisgrat mountain station at 2,900 metres in just eleven minutes. From there, the Schaufeljochbahn cable car continues to the Schaufeljoch pass at 3,170 metres above sea level. Here, the spectacular TOP OF TYROL summit platform juts out nine metres over the open rock face, offering an awe-inspiring 360-degree panoramic vista across the Stubai Alps all the way to the Dolomites. Another mesmerizing natural attraction is the Stubai Glacier Ice Grotto situated near the Eisgrat station: roughly 30 metres beneath the ski piste, visitors stroll through a 200-metre loop carved straight into ancient glacial ice, learning about glacial milk, moraines, and crevasse formation via interactive displays. During the winter months, the resort boasts 26 modern cableways and lifts, 35 diverse ski runs, the renowned Stubai Zoo snowpark, and the exhilarating ten-kilometre valley descent Wilde Grub’n.

Visit & Arrival

The Stubai Glacier offers ski operations from October well into early summer; the Top of Tyrol summit platform and the Ice Grotto are also accessible during the summer hiking season from July to September. Day ski pass for adults in peak season approx. €65.00, youth approx. €45.50, children approx. €32.50, children under 10 free when accompanied by a paying parent. Pedestrian summer ascent and descent approx. €38.00, ice grotto admission approx. €7.00. Arriving by car: take the Brenner motorway A13 to the Schönberg/Stubaital exit, continue on the B183 Stubaitalstraße valley road for roughly 32 kilometres to the spacious parking facilities at the Mutterberg valley terminal. By public transit: regional bus line 590 departs Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof every 30 minutes, running directly to the Stubai Glacier valley station.

Tips

At altitudes above 3,000 metres, alpine conditions and rapid temperature changes can occur even at the height of summer—sturdy hiking boots, warm weather-resistant layers, and UV-filtering sunglasses are indispensable. The Schaufelspitz restaurant at the Eisgrat station serves acclaimed gourmet dining high above the clouds.
preis: Adult day ski pass from approx. €65.00, summer round-trip cable car approx. €38.00
oeffnungszeiten: Ski operations Oct–May 08:00–16:30; summer alpine season July–Sept
